_comment: Turnaround baseline (road-to-agent-turnaround Phase 1.2/1.3). Produced by src/scripts/probe_turnaround.ts, NOT by the throwaway script that wrote agents/evidence/analysis/agent-turnaround-2026-08-30.md — see `instrument_vs_source` below, which records where the two disagree and why. EMPTY-CORPUS BEHAVIOUR, the whole of step 1.3: `empty_corpus: "fail"`, and the probe is deliberately NOT wired into `task ci` or any workflow. A transcript store is machine-local — `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-cwd>/*.jsonl` — so a fresh CI checkout has none, and a gate over it would be green-because-empty, which is the gate-that-scans-nothing-exits-green failure this repository names in src/config/gate-coverage.yml. Fail-closed plus local-only is the pair: the flag refuses an empty corpus rather than certifying it, and nothing schedules it where the corpus is always empty. Re-run it by hand, or from `task preflight` on a machine that has a store. THE MEASURING SESSION IS EXCLUDED, and that is correctness rather than hygiene: the first registered baseline (81.42) failed its own re-run minutes later at 81.61, because the probe was reading its own execution — API calls accumulating in the newest transcript against a user-request denominator of one. With the exclusion, two consecutive runs report 72.67 identically. `--include-current` opts back in for an offline corpus nobody is writing to.

corpus.window: the 10 most recently modified sessions in this package's transcript store, EXCLUDING the measuring session, read 2026-08-30
corpus.note: The corpus is a MOVING WINDOW by construction — `--limit 10` over mtime — so a re-run is never the same ten sessions. That is why the baseline records the window's shape (sessions, requests, calls) alongside the ratios: a ratio that moves because the denominator changed is not a regression, and without the shape nobody can tell the two apart.

directions.calls_per_request: REPORTED ONLY, not compared. Measured unstable twice for reasons that are not regressions: 81.42 -> 72.67 when the measuring session was excluded, then 72.67 -> 73.73 within the same afternoon because the corpus is an mtime window and concurrent sessions in the same project store slide into it. A ratchet on a number that moves when nothing changed teaches a reader to ignore the gate. The recorded value stays as the reference reading.
directions.mean_batch_size: UP — 1.00 is fully serial, so a HIGHER number is the improvement

instrument_vs_source.context_floor: AGREES. Instrument 217,385–230,705; source analysis 218,705–230,705. The upper bound is identical and the lower differs by 0.6 %, which is the strongest available evidence that the two readers parse the same store the same way.
instrument_vs_source.blocking_share: AGREES within the window difference: 60 % here, 64 % in the source.
instrument_vs_source.mean_batch_size: DISAGREES, and this is a FINDING rather than an instrument defect. The source reports 1.00 across 3,212 tool-using messages — 'not one message in the corpus carried two tool calls'. This window reports 1.01: 27 of 2,889 tool-using requests (0.93 %) carried 2–4 tool_use blocks, spread over five sessions. Parallel calls therefore DO occur, so 1.00 was a property of that window and not a floor with a mechanism behind it. Step 2.1 turns on exactly this.
instrument_vs_source.calls_per_request: DISAGREES LARGELY — 72.67 here against 42.6 in the source — and the difference is a DENOMINATOR effect, not a regression. This window contains long autonomous runs in which one user prompt drives hundreds of calls, so `user_requests` falls (42 vs 76) while `api_calls` stays comparable (3,052 vs 3,241). The metric is sensitive to session SHAPE, which is a real limitation of it as a ratchet and is recorded here rather than smoothed over: read it together with `corpus`, and treat a movement that tracks `user_requests` as no evidence at all.

subsequent_readings.reason: road-to-turnaround-followups step 1.1 — re-read `mean_batch_size` against the 1.01 baseline after the batching obligation landed in `src/agent-src/contexts/communication/rules-auto/token-efficiency-mechanics.md` (commit af0cf0bf0, 2026-08-30 16:38:40 +0200 = 14:38:40Z).
subsequent_readings.invocation_note: The roadmap's literal command carries no `--store`, and the probe defaults to `defaultStore(process.cwd())`. This reading was taken from the `drain/turnaround-followups` worktree at /private/tmp/ac-drain10, whose slug `-private-tmp-ac-drain10` names no directory — so the bare command measures ZERO sessions and exits 1 on `empty_corpus: "fail"`, correctly. `--store` was pointed at the store the FIRST reading measured, because a delta against a different corpus is not a delta.

corpus.window: the 10 most recently modified sessions in this package's transcript store, EXCLUDING the measuring session (dropped by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID 90ddc54d…, which the host exported), read 2026-08-30 ~20:20Z
corpus.note: THE TEN-POST-CHANGE-SESSION PRECONDITION IS NOT MET, and this is the reading's principal finding rather than a caveat on it — risk 2 of the roadmap that ordered this step predicted exactly it. By first-transcript-timestamp, ONE of the ten sessions (4fb84fae, first 16:25:33Z) began after the obligation landed at 14:38:40Z; two more (25ee3009 13:05→18:43Z, d116c1ff 11:46→16:08Z) span the moment; the remaining SEVEN ended entirely before it. Stronger still: `grep -rl` over `~/.claude` finds the obligation's text in NO installed tree — not `~/.claude/rules/token-efficiency.md` (mtime 2026-08-25), not the marketplace plugin copy — only in two transcripts, one of which is the session that authored it. The only delivered copy is the main checkout's own projection (mtime 2026-08-30 16:39), reachable on demand via `load_context` and not otherwise. So the count of sessions that could have RECEIVED the obligation is not 'fewer than ten'; on the evidence available it is at most the one that started after 14:38:40Z, and possibly zero.
corpus.shape_addition: `tool_using_requests` is recorded here and is NOT in the first entry's corpus block. It is added because without it the ratio is not reproducible from the entry — and the first entry demonstrates the cost: its `tool_calls: 3031` over the 2,889 tool-using requests its own § E2 reports gives 1.05, not the 1.01 it registers. The two figures came from different runs. A corpus block exists so a reader can recompute the ratio; this one can be recomputed (3266 / 3237 = 1.008959 → 1.01).

delta_vs_baseline.mean_batch_size: NULL — 1.01 → 1.01, the pre-committed outcome. Unrounded 1.008959 against a first reading whose unrounded value was not recorded. The finer signal moved the same way and no further: multi-block requests were 27 of 2,889 (0.93 %) and are now 26 of 3,237 (0.80 %) — 24 of size 2, one of size 3, one of size 4. The step pre-committed to this being the RESULT, not a reason to repeat the reminder more loudly; that pre-commitment binds even harder here, because the corpus could not have received the reminder in the first place.
delta_vs_baseline.blocking_share: +0.0439 — 0.6202 → 0.6641, which the gate reports as a REGRESSION and is why the run exits 1. DELIBERATELY NOT RE-BASELINED. It is not this step's metric, raising a baseline needs its own reason in its own change, and this is one local mtime-window reading.
delta_vs_baseline.context_floor_max: -4,177 — 230,705 → 226,528, within the baseline in the gated direction (DOWN). DELIBERATELY NOT LOWERED: a ratchet is never tightened on a single local reading.
delta_vs_baseline.calls_per_request: 72.67 → 93.74. REPORTED ONLY, and the movement is the denominator again exactly as `directions` records: `api_calls` is comparable (3,052 → 3,281) while `user_requests` fell 42 → 35. Evidence of nothing.
